title: llm-prefetch-routing-personal-scratchpad-priya-ramesh
content:
Goal: collect quick ideas and user stories for a prefetch + routing feature that reduces cold KV/cache misses and improves p50/p95 for common chat workloads. Rough PRD outline and open questions below.

Context
- Observed: for many customers we see heavy tail of requests that start new contexts or long-form prompts -> KV cache miss and latency spikes.
- Current options: batching, static routing to larger models, fallback tiers. None directly anticipate next token accesses across sessions.
- Idea: predictive prefetching of KV cache + routing signals to warm cheap replicas or L2 cache before primary infer call.

Non-goals
- This is not model training / RL stuff. No changes to model weights here.
- Not a replacement for long-term persistent state store (that’s separate).

Feature sketch (high-level)
- Input signals: recent user history, prompt prefix heuristics, per-customer access patterns, route-level metadata (app, locale, conversation type).
- Prefetch targets: KV cache entries for top-k probable next tokens/blocks; small fast embeddings for rerank; warm smaller quantized model variant.
- Routing actions: route predicted next-chunk requests to warm pool/dedicated node; if not confident, prefetch to shared L2 cache only.
- SLOs: aim for 5-15% reduction in per-request p95 for test workloads (chat-like). Target no more than 5% additional steady-state cost (configurable).

User stories / acceptance criteria (rough)
- As an app engineer, I want latency p95 to drop for first-token-of-turn cases without changing my prompts, so user experience is smoother.
  - AC: end-to-end p95 reduced by X ms on benchmark dataset, error rate unchanged.
- As a platform operator, I want prefetching to be opt-in per-route and visible in Console so I can control cost.
  - AC: toggle in Console + metrics (prefetch count, hit rate, cost delta).
- As an SRE, I need safeguards so prefetch storms don't overload GPUs or burst billing.
  - AC: rate limits, circuit-breakers, backpressure to routing policy.

Architecture notes / ops model
- Prefetch controller: lightweight service that consumes request stream (sampling) and emits prefetch jobs to cache warmer. Should be colocated with routing decision plane.
- Cache warmer: writes KV entries into L1/L2 caches; must support eviction TTLs tied to request heuristics.
- Model-aware prefetch: use cheap model (quantized) to estimate next-token distribution; only prefetch heavy items with >threshold confidence. Avoid wide prefetches.

Open questions / risks
- Privacy/data: prefetch uses request content. For Private deployments we need KMS and audit; for hosted may need opt-in for PII-sensitive routes.
- Cost control: how to measure and charge prefetch work? per-prefetch token? separate metric? Need product discussion.
- Quality: unnecessary prefetches can increase cost with no benefit; need good offline eval and calibration.
- Model compatibility: not all model families expose token-prob distributions cheaply (or in constant time). Fallback heuristics required.

Small experiment plan (MVP)
- Start with synthetic chat dataset + a single customer workload: sample 5,000 convo turns, simulate prefetcher using cheap n-gram / small LM to predict next chunk.
- Metrics: prefetch hit rate, p50/p95 latency before/after, additional tokens fetched, cost estimate.
- Success criteria: hit rate >30% for predicted chunks and p95 reduction >= 10% with cost delta <= 5%.

Next steps (my to-dos)
- Sync w/ Ethan on routing policy integration and sampling hook (Jira INF-812).
- Draft Confluence doc for design + console UX (CONFLUENCE-INF-2384).
- Prototype cache-warmer stub in serving-runtime PR (linked above).

Notes to self
- Keep user control central: per-route opt-in + budget cap.
- Think about multi-tenant isolation: warm pools per-tenant vs shared (cost vs isolation).
- Revisit when we have better telemetry on prefix lengths and KV re-use patterns.

Random brainstorm bullets (quick):
- Use embeddings nearest-neighbor to predict next topic chunk and prefetch representative KV object.
- Heuristic: if last token is punctuation + short turn, increase prefetch aggressiveness (likely next turn).
- Combine with TTL decay based on conversation inactivity.
- Consider a "cold-start fast lane" where new sessions get a small warm-up profile.

End of scratchpad. Will move to a more formal PRD once experiments give signal.
